title: W3C access patterns: equivalent input with stable focus
language: Native input alternatives and identity-preserving recovery
summary: A finite learning queue uses native up/down buttons, stable IDs, explicit boundary rejection and actual undo; its wrong variant commands stale array slots.
use_when: A finite web ordering task needs click and keyboard alternatives to dragging. Focus and recovery must follow the named item through reordering.
avoid_when: Does not supply a full drag implementation or custom ARIA listbox. Do not infer screen-reader, switch, speech, native-platform support or conformance.
